description: Cadmium is a soft, silvery-white metal with symbol Cd and atomic number 48. It is chemically similar to zinc and mercury in group 12, demonstrating an oxidation state of +2 in most compounds. The average concentration of cadmium in Earth's crust is between 0.1 and 0.5 parts per million.
uses: Cadmium was historically used as a corrosion-resistant plating on steel, and cadmium compounds serve as red, orange, and yellow pigments, colorants for glass, and plastic stabilizers. It is used as a neutron poison in nuclear reactor control rods, in nickel-cadmium batteries, and in cadmium telluride solar panels, though many applications have declined due to toxicity concerns.
characteristics: Cadmium is a soft, malleable, ductile, silvery-white metal that is resistant to corrosion and insoluble in water in bulk form. It burns in air to form brown amorphous cadmium oxide and is not flammable in bulk, though its powdered form may burn and release toxic fumes. Naturally occurring cadmium is composed of eight isotopes, two of which are radioactive.
